- Sleep outside on a private terrace under the stars at La Valise Tulum, an SLH Hotel or experience university history and traditions at Graduate by Hilton Princeton.

Some destinations are unforgettable. So are the Stays that bring them to life. From spending a night under the stars in Tulum, Mexico, to exploring an ancient castle in the Old Town of Cáceres, Spain that brims with history, here are just six unique Stay experiences.


## **La Valise Tulum, an SLH Hotel — Mexico**


[La Valise Tulum, an SLH Hotel](https://www.hilton.com/en/hotels/cunlvlx-la-valise-tulum/) is nestled between the Caribbean Sea and the Mayan jungle at Carr and is split into two wings: one with 11 rooms offering beachside suites, the other with 11 jungle-view suites. Just one of the hotel’s unforgettable highlights are the moveable king-size roll-out beds that let guests sleep indoors—or outside on their private terraces under the stars. During the day, guests can dine at NÜ in Tulum, with intimate private dining, curated mezcal tastings, immersive cooking classes, and more.


## **Graduate by Hilton Princeton — New Jersey**


Located directly across from Princeton University's campus on historic Nassau Street,[Graduate by Hilton Princeton](https://www.hilton.com/en/hotels/pctgpgu-graduate-princeton/) occupies a meticulously restored and expanded 1918-era student dormitory. When it opened in 2024, the 180-room property marked the first new hotel to open in Princeton in nearly 90 years, with interiors filled with playful references to the university's history and traditions. In the Gothic-inspired lobby, guests are greeted by carved wooden tiger mascots, a 30-foot communal study table and vintage Princeton Senior Jackets. Guest rooms feature bedside lamps inspired by a Revolutionary War-era cannon buried behind Nassau Hall, while the hotel's signature restaurant, Ye Tavern, takes its name from a 1930s bar that once occupied the site.


## **Waldorf Astoria Los Cabos Pedregal — Mexico**


Reached through Mexico’s only privately owned Dos Mares tunnel,[Waldorf Astoria Los Cabos Pedregal](https://www.waldorfastorialoscabospedregal.com/) occupies a secluded 24-acre enclave where the Pacific meets the southern tip of Baja California. A recent, resort-wide transformation brought new depth to the guest experience, with 112 redesigned accommodations shaped by the artistry of Mexico. Textiles, sculpture, furniture and works by artisans from Oaxaca, Baja California Sur, Jalisco and beyond lend each space a distinctive sense of place. That connection continues at the table and in the spa: TRAVESÍA reimagines the taco in a nine-course tasting menu, while treatments draw on Mexico’s folk-healing traditions. The result is a rare expression of seclusion and refinement, grounded in the creativity and character of its setting.


## ****Palacio de Godoy Cáceres, Curio** **Collection** **by** **Hilton** **— Spain****


The historic[Palacio de Godoy Cáceres, Curio Collection by Hilton](https://www.hilton.com/en/hotels/bjzpgqq-palacio-de-godoy-caceres/) , located within the UNESCO-listed Old Town of Cáceres, occupies a restored 16th-century palace that was originally built by Francisco de Godoy, a conquistador and founder of Lima, Peru. Mamay Aldana serves up Mediterranean cuisine is for breakfast, lunch, dinner and drinks, and its Palacio Ritual Spa offers a heated pool, sauna, and hammam. Located three and a half hours of Madrid and Lisbon, the hotel makes a great destination for a long weekend enjoying the hotel or exploring the nearby Concatedral de Santa Maria de Cáceres, Palace of Los Golfines De Abajo or Plaza Mayor de Caceres. (Eagle-eyed guests may also recognize locations in Cáceres’ Old Town from an award-winning streaming series adapted from a book, including its 12th-century Moorish walls, 14th- to 16th-century fortress houses and Gothic churches).


Its gardens, designed by Álvaro de la Rosa, combine native plants with American species, evoking the gardens of 16th- and 17th-century Lima. Signature restaurant Mamay Aldana pays tribute to Godoy's mother, María de Aldana, through cuisine celebrating the region's culinary heritage, while rooftop Bar Virú offers views of the historic city and surrounding Extremadura countryside.


## ******The Radical Asheville, Tapestry Collection by Hilton** **— North Carolina******


Housed in a converted 1920s cereal factory warehouse,[The Radical Asheville, Tapestry Collection by Hilton](https://www.hilton.com/en/hotels/avlupup-the-radical-asheville/) is a living art installation that blends industrial grit with posh-meets-punk interior design and vibrant street art. The Radical features 70 rooms and brings together reclaimed materials, street art and avant-garde design to create a stay that feels both rebellious and refined, boldly reflecting the city's creative energy and artistic spirit. Located in the River Arts District of Asheville, the hotel is home to Golden Hour, its flagship restaurant that offers a farm-to-table menu created by a James Beard-nominated chef. Guests can enjoy locally inspired dishes and striking gathering spaces filled with murals and installations, while after/glow, the property’s cafe and bar, offers another casual place to gather. Upstairs, The Roof, a rooftop bar, offers views of the French Broad River.


## ********Maison Heler Metz, Curio Collection by Hilton —** **France********


The imaginative, castle-like design of[Maison Heler Metz, Curio Collection by Hilton](https://www.hilton.com/en/hotels/etzmhqq-maison-heler-metz/) was inspired by La Vie Minutieuse de Manfred Heler (The Meticulous Life of Manfred Heler), a fictional novel written by designer Philippe Starck. The story follows an eccentric inventor whose home and park are mysteriously lifted high above the city while he daydreams. Starck brings this story to life through the hotel's architecture, with a traditional Lorraine-style chalet perched atop a modern concrete tower.


Opened in March 2025, Maison Heler Metz brings Philippe Starck’s imaginative approach to design to the French city of Metz. The hotel features 104 rooms and suites within a nine-story Brutalist-style structure topped by a house inspired by traditional Lorraine architecture. Complementing its distinctive architecture, the hotel offers La Cuisine de Rose, a garden-level brasserie, and La Maison de Manfred, a rooftop restaurant and bar offering panoramic views of the city. Situated in Metz’s Amphitheatre district, the property is within walking distance of the Centre Pompidou-Metz and the city center.


##### FAQ: Explore New Ways to Stay with Hilton


A few of the unique Stays travelers can experience with Hilton include La Valise Tulum, an SLH Hotel; Graduate by Hilton Princeton; Waldorf Astoria Los Cabos Pedregal; Palacio de Godoy Cáceres, Curio Collection by Hilton; The Radical Asheville, Tapestry Collection by Hilton; and Maison Heler Metz, Curio Collection by Hilton.


Graduate by Hilton Princeton occupies a meticulously restored and expanded 1918-era student dormitory; Palacio de Godoy Cáceres, Curio Collection by Hilton occupies a restored 16th-century palace; The Radical Asheville, Tapestry Collection by Hilton is housed in a converted 1920s cereal factory warehouse; and Maison Heler Metz, Curio Collection by Hilton features a traditional Lorraine-style chalet perched atop a modern concrete tower.


Guests can sleep indoors or outside on their private terraces under the stars at La Valise Tulum, an SLH Hotel; enjoy a nine-course tasting menu at TRAVESÍA at Waldorf Astoria Los Cabos Pedregal; explore the UNESCO-listed Old Town of Cáceres from Palacio de Godoy Cáceres, Curio Collection by Hilton; enjoy locally inspired dishes and striking gathering spaces filled with murals and installations at The Radical Asheville, Tapestry Collection by Hilton; and take in panoramic views of the city from La Maison de Manfred at Maison Heler Metz, Curio Collection by Hilton.
